person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: microplastics and the chemical additives they carry - A CLASS DEFINED BY A SIZE RANGE AND NOTHING ELSE, and what it does to human bodies
span.quote: Microplastics (MPs) are defined by [ 17 ] as “synthetic solid particles or polymeric matrices, with regular or irregular shape and with size ranging from 1 μm to 5 mm, of either primary or secondary manufacturing origin, which are insoluble in water.

span.label: which additives in plastic are hazardous, whether microplastics act as vectors carrying them into the body, and by what route they enter
span.quote: Microplastics can contain two types of chemicals: (i) additives and polymeric raw materials (e.g., monomers or oligomers) originating from the plastics, and (ii) chemicals absorbed from the surrounding ambience.

span.label: a review of the additives of concern and of the exposure pathways - ingestion, inhalation, skin - with the size threshold each barrier imposes
span.quote: Not enough information is available to fully understand the implications of microplastics for human health; however, effects may potentially be due to their physical properties (size, shape, and length), chemical properties (presence of additives and polymer type), concentration, or microbial biofilm growth.

span.label: critique
span.quote: Not enough information is available to fully understand the implications of microplastics for human health; however, effects may potentially be due to their physical properties (size, shape, and length), chemical properties (presence of additives and polymer type), concentration, or microbial biofilm growth.

span.label: plastic fragmenting to particles small enough to cross biological barriers, while carrying additives that are not chemically bound to the polymer and can leach
span.quote: The additives, in almost all cases, are not chemically bound to the plastic polymer; only some flame retardants are polymerized with plastic molecules, becoming part of the polymeric chain

span.label: narrative review of the literature on micro and nanoplastic exposure pathways and additive toxicity; no new measurement
span.term: narrative review of the literature on micro and nanoplastic exposure pathways and additive toxicity; no new measurement
span.quote: Not enough information is available to fully understand the implications of microplastics for human health; however, effects may potentially be due to their physical properties (size, shape, and length), chemical properties (presence of additives and polymer type), concentration, or microbial biofilm growth.

span.label: THE CLASS IS A SIZE RANGE AND NOTHING ELSE: microplastics are `synthetic solid particles ... WITH SIZE RANGING FROM 1 um TO 5 mm ... which are insoluble in water`. Composition, origin and shape are all left open - `regular or irregular shape`, `either primary or secondary manufacturing origin`. ONLY THE TWO NUMBERS ARE BINDING
span.quote: Microplastics (MPs) are defined by [ 17 ] as “synthetic solid particles or polymeric matrices, with regular or irregular shape and with size ranging from 1 μm to 5 mm, of either primary or secondary manufacturing origin, which are insoluble in water.

span.label: and the class below it ABUTS IT EXACTLY: nanoplastics are `particles that are UNINTENTIONALLY PRODUCED within the size range FROM 1 TO 1000 nm`. 1000 nm IS 1 um. The boundary between the two classes is one number with nothing behind it - AND THE NANOPLASTIC DEFINITION SMUGGLES IN A CRITERION THAT IS NOT PHYSICAL AT ALL: a 500 nm particle made on purpose is not a nanoplastic under it, and an identical one made by accident is
span.quote: The authors of [ 111 ] observed the Pb absorption capacity on nanoplastics (particles that are unintentionally produced within the size range from 1 to 1000 nm [ 113 ]) that were produced from microplastics that were collected on a beach exposed to the North Atlantic Gyre.

span.label: the additives are NOT PART OF THE PLASTIC: `the additives, in almost all cases, ARE NOT CHEMICALLY BOUND to the plastic polymer; only some flame retardants are polymerized with plastic molecules, becoming part of the polymeric chain`. That is why a particle can act as a vector - what it carries can leave it
span.quote: The additives, in almost all cases, are not chemically bound to the plastic polymer; only some flame retardants are polymerized with plastic molecules, becoming part of the polymeric chain

span.label: and EVERY BARRIER HAS ITS OWN NUMBER: <150 um crosses the gastrointestinal epithelium, <2.5 um enters by endocytosis through M cells, <100 nm penetrates the corneous layer of skin, ~20 um penetrates organs and ~10 um reaches all of them. THE BIOLOGY IS A LADDER OF SIZE THRESHOLDS, and the class boundary at 1 um sits in the middle of it rather than at any of them
span.quote: Once ingested, particles smaller than 2.5 μm can enter the gastrointestinal tract ( Figure 6 ) through endocytosis by M cells (specialized epithelial cells of the mucosa-associated lymphoid tissues) of Peyer

span.label: THE PAPER REPRODUCES A NUMBER ITS OWN DEFINITION EXCLUDES. Nine thousand words after defining microplastics as `1 um to 5 mm`, it reports `the finding of microplastics into human stools: Twenty plastic particles, mostly PE and PP (RANGING IN SIZE BETWEEN 5 AND 500 mm)`. 500 mm IS HALF A METRE. EVERY PARTICLE IN THAT RANGE IS OUTSIDE THE CLASS THE SENTENCE CALLS IT A MEMBER OF. I checked the publisher's XML before saying it: `between 5 and 500 mm` is verbatim in the source, and the same file renders the micro sign correctly eleven times elsewhere, SO IT IS NOT THE PIPELINE
span.quote: This assumption, regarding levels of microplastics in men at a gastro-intestinal level, was further confirmed by the finding of microplastics into human stools: Twenty plastic particles, mostly PE and PP (ranging in size between 5 and 500 mm), were found for every 10 g of stool

span.label: the review states four separate things it does not know, in four consecutive sentences of its own conclusion: the fate and effects are `STILL CONTROVERSIAL AND NOT WELL KNOWN`; `NOT ENOUGH INFORMATION is available to fully understand the implications`; how chemicals adsorb and desorb `IS NOT WELL KNOWN`; and the primary sources of the pollutants on the particles are unexplained
span.quote: Following the intake of microplastics into the human body, their fate and effects are still controversial and not well known.

span.label: AND THE ABSENCE IS ATTRIBUTED TO THE INSTRUMENT, NOT TO THE WORLD: `data about micro and nanoplastics into the environment are still limited DUE TO THE ANALYTICAL AND TECHNICAL COMPLICATIONS TO EXTRACT, CHARACTERIZE, AND QUANTIFY THEM from environmental matrices`. The class is hard to measure, so the exposure figures are predictions
span.quote: Exposure concentrations are predicted to be low, although data about micro and nanoplastics into the environment are still limited due to the analytical and technical complications to extract, characterize, and quantify them from environmental matrices

span.label: the vector hypothesis - the paper's own framing - is UNRESOLVED AND ITS ONE CITED EXPERIMENT POINTS THE OTHER WAY: `the combination of BPA and PA led to DECREASED immobilization` and `the LOWER BPA body burden of daphnids IN THE PRESENCE of PA particles`. The particles reduced the toxicity of the chemical they were supposed to be delivering
span.quote: The combination of BPA and PA led to decreased immobilization, although the daphnids ingested PA particles that were loaded with BPA. These results showed the lower BPA body burden of daphnids in the presence of PA particles.

span.label: and two of its own retention figures sit oddly together: `only 0.3% of these particles are expected to be absorbed` against `the human excretory system should be responsible for removing UP TO 90%`. Different denominators are possible and neither sentence states its own, WHICH IS THE PROBLEM
span.quote: Indeed, the human excretory system should be responsible for removing up to 90% of micro and nanoplastics ingested

span.label: the daphnid experiment the review recounts: PA particles alone, BPA alone, and the two combined, with a fixed particle concentration and varying BPA
span.note: eliminates: the particle itself as a toxicant - `PA particles alone did not induce adverse effects, while the effects of BPA alone followed a typical dose-dependent manner` · outcome: held
span.quote: It is still under discussion if microplastics are relevant pollutant vectors for uptake into organisms in comparison to further uptake pathways, e.g., via water or sediment particles, even if studies regarding the level of bisphenol A adhered on microplastics surface are very limited.

span.label: whether the size range the review quotes for its own headline human finding is inside the class it defined
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the definition is `1 um to 5 mm` and the stool particles are quoted at `BETWEEN 5 AND 500 mm`, entirely above it. The review does not notice · outcome: failed

span.note: eliminates: nothing, and the paper says so about the definitions it inherited: `THESE DEFINITIONS ARE CONFUSING AND MISLEADING DUE TO THE FACT THAT THEY CAUSE THE INCLUSION OF NON-METALS`. The failure is what motivates the enumeration · outcome: failed
span.quote: Heavy metals are natural elements that have a relatively high atomic mass and a rather high density compared to water. Commonly, a density of at least 5 g/cm −3 defines a heavy metal and differentiates it from other “light” metals. Other, broader definitions for “heavy metals” require an atomic mass higher than 23 or an atomic number exceeding 20 [ 75 , 76 , 77 ]. However, these definitions are confusing and misleading due to the fact that they cause the inclusion of non-metals.
